claim_a.quote: Every data store in the Meridian platform is encrypted at rest under customer-managed KMS keys per our encryption standard — RDS, S3, ElastiCache, all of it. Encryption is table stakes and we treat it that way.

resolution: The memo overstates. Three PHI-bearing buckets — meridian-db-snapshots, meridian-legacy-exports, and meridian-data-lake-raw — sit on the account-default SSE-S3 key, not the customer-managed KMS keys the memo claims and POL-09 requires. meridian-db-snapshots also has public-access-block disabled, and account-default encryption gates nothing: Graphite Wren read plaintext PHI snapshots from it with the leaked over-permissive IAM key (VB-2026-C1). The runbook confirms the bucket was carved out of the 2024 KMS migration and never migrated back.
why_decidable: The bucket inventory is a raw system export dated 2026-06-08 (Gideon Hart's cover note marks it as pulled directly from the AWS API); the memo is undated narrative prose. Export beats assertion; the runbook and the pen-test critical independently confirm both the off-standard key and the exploitability.

claim_a.quote: User access reviews are performed quarterly for all production systems, with results documented and exceptions remediated within 30 days.

claim_b.quote: the last full access review anyone actually finished was September 2025 — IT-3312 is still sitting unassigned in the queue.

resolution: The quarterly cadence lapsed after the Type I. The 2026-06-08 access export shows last_reviewed values of 2025-09 across production systems and three departed employees still active. The Type I described control design as of 2025-06-30, not current operation.
why_decidable: The access export carries per-row last_reviewed dates and active flags — current-state system evidence. The Type I is a point-in-time design opinion eleven months stale; its own cover language limits it to 2025-06-30.

claim_a.quote: Multi-factor authentication is enforced for 100% of remote access to production systems.

claim_b.quote: legacy Fortinet VPN (vpn2.meridianhl.example) — local accounts, password auth only; MFA rollout deferred to 'post-migration'.

resolution: The questionnaire overstates. Okta-fronted apps do enforce MFA, but the legacy VPN — which reaches the production VPC — is password-only, and 14 users (per the access export vpn2 rows) hold local VPN accounts. Graphite Wren's password-spray critical proves exploitability.
why_decidable: The runbook is the engineering team's operational configuration record and matches both the access export (auth_method=password rows for vpn2) and the pen-test finding; the questionnaire is a sales artifact with no evidence attached.

claim_a.quote: Our most recent third-party penetration test identified no critical findings; all issues were remediated within SLA.

claim_b.quote: Two (2) Critical findings remain open as of 2026-05-30: VB-2026-C1 (unauthenticated read access to meridian-db-snapshots via an over-permissive IAM access key) and VB-2026-C2 (successful password spray against vpn2 local accounts).

resolution: Two criticals are open. Note the sequencing nuance: the questionnaire (April) predates the Graphite Wren report (May 30), but the questionnaire referenced the 2024 test and asserted a clean posture Meridian could not evidence; either way the answer on file with Bayview is now materially false and needs correcting.
why_decidable: The pen-test executive summary is the third-party tester's own dated report with finding IDs; the questionnaire cites no report and Gideon Hart's cover email states no 2025 test occurred at all.

claim_a.quote: All subprocessors with PHI access are disclosed to customers and operate under executed BAAs.

claim_b.quote: Their legal redlined the BAA in November and we never countersigned — there is nothing executed on file for Mercury.

resolution: Mercury Messaging — the SMS aggregator carrying every PHI-bearing text — has no executed BAA (register status 'In negotiation — sent 2025-11-04, not countersigned') and subprocessor_disclosed=No, while the Bayview BAA §5.2 requires prior written disclosure and BAA flow-down for every subcontractor handling PHI. Meridian is in breach of that clause today.
why_decidable: The vendor register's baa_status and subprocessor_disclosed columns are the compliance system of record, and the email thread from the vendor negotiation itself confirms non-execution; the memo offers no document reference.

claim_a.quote: The disaster recovery plan is tested at least annually, and test results are reviewed by management.

claim_b.quote: [00:41:07] We have never actually run a failover test. Not once. The DR doc is from 2023 and half the runbook steps reference infrastructure we've already replaced.

resolution: Never tested. The policy (last reviewed 2024-03) and the Castlewick Type I both describe annual testing that has never occurred; no test artifact exists anywhere in the evidence set, and #eng-infra jokes about it ('lol no').
why_decidable: An against-interest admission by the accountable executive, corroborated by the total absence of test records and the Slack exchange; the policy claim is design language never operationalized.

claim_a.quote: All new hires complete security awareness training within 30 days of start; every employee completes an annual refresher.

resolution: Only 29 of 45 (64.4%) have completed the 2026 cycle as of June; the checklist is aspirational. Sixteen employees, including two engineers with production access, are outstanding.
why_decidable: The tracker is a per-employee LMS export with completion dates; the checklist is an unversioned process aspiration whose offboarding half is explicitly marked DRAFT.

claim_a.quote: Meridian Health Loop has grown to more than 50 employees across three states.

claim_b.quote: # active employees: 45 (5 terminated rows retained for audit)

resolution: 45 active employees as of 2026-06-01. The press release counted contractors and pre-attrition headcount at funding announcement; the payroll roster is authoritative for system-description and coverage denominators.
why_decidable: A dated payroll export with per-row status beats a marketing figure from ten months earlier; Rosa Delgado's cover email confirms 45 active.

topic: How many employees are on unmanaged personal laptops

claim_a.quote: its rly not a big deal, only like 3 people are still on personal laptops, everyone else got corp machines last year

resolution: Eight, not three: 45 active employees minus 37 enrolled corporate devices = 8 unmanaged BYOD users (sales plus part of CS). Tom's interview corroborates the population ('sales and a chunk of CS') and points to the Kandji export as the real number.
why_decidable: Arithmetic on two dated system exports (roster and MDM) beats a junior engineer's off-hand Slack estimate; the VP Engineering explicitly defers to the export.

claim_a.quote: We commit to a 99.99% uptime SLA for all customers.

claim_b.quote: Provider will maintain Platform availability of no less than 99.9% Monthly Uptime, measured per §7.3, with service credits per Schedule C.

resolution: The executed MSA says 99.9%; the questionnaire's 99.99% is an unsupported overstatement (a 10x tighter downtime budget than anything Meridian has committed to or measured). The readiness report should anchor the Availability scope on 99.9%.
why_decidable: An executed contract excerpt with section numbers versus an unsourced sales answer; Ruth Okonjo's questionnaire follow-up email even asks Meridian to reconcile the two numbers.
